dedupe_keys.name: san antonio smartsa pilot street light sensor data

description: This dataset holds readings from the SmartSA smart streetlight pilot, which fitted remote lighting controls and environmental sensors to up to 40 streetlights in each of three innovation zones, Downtown, Brooks and the Medical Center, for up to 120 in all. The pilot tested five uses chosen by city stakeholders: air quality, temperature, ambient noise, parking availability and flood level sensing, to judge whether smart streetlights are worth scaling city-wide. The portal has, for each zone, air quality, flood, sound level and weather CSV files, plus data dictionaries for particulates, weather, noise and water level. Coverage: three districts of San Antonio, Texas. Access: free from the city open data portal. Licence: Creative Commons Attribution, with a disclaimer that the data are provided as is. Caveats: a short pilot with few poles per zone; no parking data files were seen among the resources. Simulation uses are street-scale heat and flood sensing inputs for public space digital twins, and tests of streetlight poles as sensor platforms. Related records: the FIWARE Smart Data Models streetlighting schema.
